title: The auth filter is an exclusion list of routes: every path added for a reason is unauthenticated by construction
index_line: T-0055 · EXEC · 58 endpoints excluded from the auth filter, one of them deploys a ZIP · java · corroborated
invariant_violated: Authentication is assumed to be on by default with a few deliberate holes for endpoints that must work before login. But a filter written as a list of exceptions inverts the default: safety becomes a property of not being on the list, and the list only grows. Each addition was reasonable in isolation, and one of them is a code path with real power.

mechanism.does: the attacker enumerates routes on the management portal and finds those answered without a session
the route table is filtered by an exclusion list, so 58 endpoints never reach the authentication check
one excluded endpoint accepts an uploaded package and expands it on the server
the archive's member paths are honoured on expansion, so content lands outside the intended directory
a written component is loaded by the application on the next start or request

source.http.request.value: a POST to an excluded route — no credentials, and the route is found by enumeration rather than the UI

guard.none.value: the exclusion list itself: the guard is per-route and defaults to absent

sink.file.write.value: the package expansion writing archive members to disk

encoding.path.value: member names inside the archive deciding where each file lands

preconditions.expr: authentication is enforced by a filter that lists excluded paths
an excluded route performs a write or deployment action

spec.method: request each excluded route without a cookie and record which return non-auth responses with side effects

success: an unauthenticated POST to the deployment route returns a task/acceptance response instead of a redirect to login
a file appears on the server from an archive supplied in that request
the enumeration of all excluded routes is a finding by itself — list them
failure_like: the filter defaults to deny and enumerates what needs authentication
the deployment route validates a signed package or a shared secret
false_positive: a login, health or static route answering unauthenticated — that is the design
a 302 to the login page read as success: check the body and the side effect

hazards: the audit artefact is the exclusion list: dump it and diff it against the routes that actually do work
every framework has this construct (Spring shouldNotFilter, servlet url-patterns, Express ordering, permitAll) — read it as attack surface, not config
deploy, restore and import routes are the ones to read first: they were excluded because another system calls them, and they write files
distinct from T-0051 (a guard inside a conditional) and T-0046 (a guard simply absent): here the guard is deliberately bypassed per route
non_transfers: default-deny filter chains with an explicit allow-list of methods rather than paths
deployment routes that require a signed artefact
